Support.text: Open source CMS developed and maintained by the WordPress contributor community.

Technology.text:
Server: PHP.
Database: MySQL or MariaDB.
Browser: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.

Capabilities.text: Themes and block editing let users customize website layouts and publish content.
Plugins extend the CMS with additional website functionality.

Limitations.text: Outdated or vulnerable plugins can expose the website to attacks. Administrators must maintain updates and remove unused plugins.
Poorly implemented plugins or themes can cause excessive database activity. Under heavy traffic, excessive database connections can overload the server and reduce website performance.

Support.text: Open source CMS developed by the Drupal community, with community infrastructure and project support from the Drupal Association.

Technology.text:
Server: PHP.
Database: MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, or SQLite.
Browser: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.

Capabilities.text: Custom content types and fields support structured content beyond basic blog posts.
Modules and themes extend functionality and appearance. User roles and permissions control access to content and administration.

Limitations.text: Major version upgrades require compatible contributed modules, themes, and custom code. Deprecated APIs must be identified and corrected before upgrading.
The core upgrade path does not support skipping major versions. A website several major versions behind must complete successive major upgrades.

Support.text: Open source CMS developed by the Joomla volunteer community and supported organizationally by Open Source Matters.

Technology.text:
Server: PHP.
Database: MySQL, MariaDB, or PostgreSQL.
Browser: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.

Capabilities.text: Built in multilingual content management and access controls support websites with multiple languages and user groups.
Templates customize website appearance, while components, modules, and plugins add functionality.

Limitations.text: Third party extension incompatibility can block major version upgrades or require removing functionality. For Joomla 5 to 6, extensions must no longer depend on Joomla 5's backward compatibility plugin.

Support.text: Open source publishing software maintained by the nonprofit Ghost Foundation. Ghost(Pro) provides paid managed hosting.

Technology.text:
Server: JavaScript.
Database: MySQL.
Browser: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.

Capabilities.text: Built in publishing tools support posts, pages, and email newsletters.
Memberships and paid subscriptions support subscriber only content. APIs allow external applications and custom front ends to access content.

Limitations.text: Stripe is the only natively supported payment provider. Publishers unable to use Stripe cannot use the standard native payment setup, another provider requires third party automation or a custom API integration.

Support.text: Open source CMS supported by its developer community. Professional services are available from Trilby Media.

Technology.text:
Server: PHP with Twig templates.
Database: None required, content and configuration use Markdown and YAML files.
Browser: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.

Capabilities.text: Themes, plugins, and Twig templates support custom layouts and extended functionality.
Flat file content storage and multilingual support allow websites to be managed without setting up a database.

Limitations.text: File based page change detection can slow large websites. Disabling automatic change checking improves production performance, but changed pages no longer automatically trigger that cache refresh.
Performance depends heavily on PHP caching and filesystem speed. The documentation identifies PHP caching as critical and advises against network filesystems such as NFS.
